summary: X14's 'impossible' is an overreach; solver market structure is mis-shelved as weather rather than a designed object; the Value 'conservation law' is residual accounting, not an invariant with predictive content.

findings.claim: Solver exclusivity + a claim of competitive price improvement is classed 'Impossible' because exclusivity removes the live counterfactual.
findings.problem: Economically false as stated. Exclusivity removes contemporaneous multi-solver rivalry on that order, not all competitive content. Price improvement remains definable and enforceable against an external benchmark (mid, TWAP, batch uniform price), via franchise bidding for exclusive slots, contestable entry, bonded SLA/reputation, or post-trade allocation of next flow. 'Impossible' confuses missing live co-solver counterfactual with impossibility of any competitive claim.
findings.fix: Reclass X14 as 'Unstable/unverifiable without named benchmark or commitment device'. Require the formula to name the counterfactual (external reference, contestability rule, or bonded improvement obligation). Reserve 'Impossible' for logical contradictions, not missing co-solver rivalry.

findings.claim: A fourth informational bond is irreducible; folding observation into the economic bond makes private-order-flow analysis unauditable; the naming clause requires naming the economic consequence.
findings.problem: The fourth type is not redundant: information structure is a first-class object in mechanism design (type/observation profile vs transfer/payoff rules), and observation can occur with no call, transfer, attestation, or pre-priced incentive link—Glosten–Milgrom/Kyle toxicity is not the same object as solvency/loss-allocation. But the document overclaims 'irreducible to a priced externality': adverse selection is routinely capitalized into spreads, batch discounts, and exclusivity premia when a residual claimant and a pricing margin exist. The naming clause almost concedes the point by requiring an economic consequence, which invites treating —n→ as a mere annotation on —e→ rather than a separate satisfaction condition.
findings.fix: Keep —n→ as a required, separately audited edge (who observes what, when, with what exclusivity). Drop 'irreducible to priced externality' rhetoric. State: observation graph ≠ incentive graph; pricing may capitalize rents ex post but does not erase the need to name the observation channel ex ante. Allow well-formed —n→ that names a rent/agency channel even when not yet a loss-allocation failure.

findings.claim: Three durable invariants (Value, Authority, Information) replace the cross-chain trilemma.
findings.problem: They are not parallel objects. Value ('destination credit = verified debit + underwritten advance − fees − allocated loss') is an accounting identity once residuals are defined by construction: any gap is re-labelled advance, fee, or allocated loss, so the equality has no out-of-sample predictive content—only a completeness discipline. Authority is a real inclusion constraint when enforcement binds. Information ('provenance/meaning must not be silently mutated') is a normative integrity rule, not conservation of any measurable stock; messages are aggregated, delayed, and re-interpreted at trust boundaries by design. Weakest: Value, as a 'law'—true by residual taxonomy, not by mechanism.
findings.fix: Relabel Value as a 'completeness / residual-assignment requirement' (model well-formedness), not a conservation law. Keep Authority as an enforceable invariant. Restate Information as a non-mutation integrity obligation with an explicit mutability allowance list (aggregation, delay, encoding)—or drop 'conservation' language entirely.

findings.section: §15 Reflexivity (hypothesis, not theorem); carried unanimously in §1
findings.claim: Reflexivity is a hypothesis, not a theorem; downgraded from SOURCE-A master predictor for lack of longitudinal coding, matched controls, and false-positive rate.
findings.problem: The downgrade is correct as a claim of calibrated taxonomic prediction. It is too weak as economics. Fire-sale externalities, leverage cycles, liquidity spirals, and endogenous-collateral feedback are standard mechanisms, not speculative lore. The triple loop (token as collateral, depth, and backstop) is a concrete amplification channel, not a free parameter. Conflating 'unvalidated as a scored screen for this table' with 'only a hypothesis about economic dynamics' understates mechanism strength and will cause designers to under-weight X1/X3/X17 relative to thinner empirical incidents.
findings.fix: Split the status: mechanism class = established (cite the feedback channel, not dollar folklore); table-level predictive instrument = uncalibrated hypothesis pending coding/FPR. Keep the ex-ante screen; stop language that treats the spiral itself as optional.

findings.claim: Solver market structure is an environmental reaction condition for In/Ba/Rf/Of: whether the resolver set is concentrated enough to sustain rents or exhaust liquidity.
findings.problem: Treating concentration as weather is a category error for intent/solver systems. Solver set size, exclusivity windows, vertical integration (solver=LP=filler), entry barriers, and surplus split are design-endogenous industrial organization—not an exogenous operating range like block time. Listing them as reaction conditions buries market power, collusion risk, and rent extraction outside valence, bonds, and bonding laws, so formulas can look well-formed while the only economically load-bearing object (who captures the informational rent) is ambient.
findings.fix: Promote solver market structure to a first-class modelled object: required parameters/isotopes on In/Ba/Rf/Of (open competition | exclusive | RFQ-permissioned | vertically integrated), plus an economic bond for surplus allocation and an X-rule for exclusivity without benchmark/commitment (ties to F1). Keep residual environment only for truly exogenous infra (chain latency, base-layer MEV regime).

findings.claim: Incentives group is essentially Em; fees appear only as a residual in the Value identity; no first-class fee distribution, cross-subsidy, principal-agent, or time-preference structure.
findings.problem: The economically load-bearing objects of DeFi microstructure are missing as elements/bonds: (i) fee/surplus distribution (LP fee, protocol fee, solver surplus, priority tips, PFOF-like order-flow payments); (ii) cross-subsidy (retail vs toxic flow, Em as LP subsidy, Gs as routed subsidy); (iii) principal-agent structure (user→solver, depositor→curator/vault, tokenholder→guardian) beyond Au's scope bounds—scope ≠ aligned incentives; (iv) time preference as a priced object outside Ft/Pf (funding, discount factors, impatience in Wq/Of). Without these, adverse selection named on —n→ has nowhere to land as a transfer rule, and 'economic bond' solvency checks cannot see who is paid to bear toxicity.
findings.fix: Add at least: a surplus-allocation bond or element (fee schedule / residual claimant), an explicit agency/incentive-alignment requirement on Au and In (not only scope/timeout), and a cross-subsidy flag where Em or Gs finances another role's economics. Put maker-taker or flow-payment channels under —e→ or —n→ with named incidence.

strongest_thing_in_the_document: Separating observation (—n→) from interface/trust/economic bonds and forcing L24 disclosure on In/Rf/Ba is the right microstructure instinct—order-flow information is not a call graph.
dissent_note: Formalists may defend X14's 'impossible' and Value-as-law as modelling hygiene; IO lenses should agree solver structure is under-modelled.
